column2: A traveller from the Far East reaches your court with a bodyguard of jade-armoured warriors. He unrolls a silk scroll and reads that the Dragon Emperor of Grand Cathay, Son of Heaven and Lord of the Ivory Road, expects a tribute of a thousand heavenly dragons from every lord whose markets grow fat on Cathayan silk.
Surely he means coin...?
Your Dragon Emperor has no power here!

Another envoy from Cathay arrives at your court. He bows low and explains that he is himself a gift, a token of the Dragon Emperor's gratitude, and that there is no finer governor of trade between here and the Great Bastion should you need one.
Let him govern the trade at [trade_province.GetName].
He can muck out the stables.
Politely decline the offer.

More and more caravans from the East stop at [trade_province.GetName] since [cathayan_envoy.GetBestName] took charge of the trade there. The market is loud with strange tongues, and the tax-men are smiling.
Let the trade flow.
[cathayan_envoy.GetBestName] has acquired a casket of rare gemstones on your behalf: jade from the Jade Sea, pearls from Haichai and a ruby the size of a quail's egg.
Sell them for profit.
These will look fine in a pendant.
Earrings for my [Root.Spouse.GetHusbandWife].
A pair of travelling merchants claim that their goods were stolen while they lodged under your roof. They want compensation, and they are loud about it.
Apologise and reimburse them.
That is their loss.
Beaming and chattering, [cathayan_envoy.GetFirstName] drags a heavy sack into the hall. He says he found these valuable goods lying about the premises, and he would like to share them with you.
I wonder if this is a coincidence...
Find the merchants and return their cargo.
[cathayan_envoy.GetBestName] enters your chamber with a new pet wrapped around his neck: a serpent with scales like green jade, thick as your arm. He asks if you would like to stroke it.
I hope it does not bite.
It seems a bit dangerous.
Forbid [cathayan_envoy.GetHerHim] from keeping the snake.
Furious barking outside! You rush into the yard just in time to see [cathayan_envoy.GetFirstName]'s jade serpent swallow your beloved [Root.GetDogName] in a single gulp.
A scream from the yard! You rush outside just in time to see [cathayan_envoy.GetFirstName]'s jade serpent swallow the hound of [ivory_hound_owner.GetTitledFirstName] in a single gulp.
Such is the way of things.
Someone slay that beast before it does more harm!
Poor [Root.GetDogName]!
I will have [cathayan_envoy.GetHerHis] head for this!

You are walking in the gardens with [ivory_envoy_bride.GetFirstName] when [cathayan_envoy.GetFirstName] approaches, bowing. By the laws of Cathay, he explains, an official who serves abroad for long must take a wife, and his eyes have settled on your companion.
Ahem... we were just discussing that, [ivory_envoy_bride.GetFirstName]. Were we not?
Then I have no more need of your services.

Dust rises in your wake as you stride into the tavern. There sits [cathayan_envoy.GetFirstName] over a game of bones and copper cups, betting your silver and losing it. He looks up with a happy smile. 'Ah! Your wine is very... very good.'
Just stay away from these people.
Arrest this [cathayan_envoy.GetManWoman].

[Root.GetTitledFirstName],

I hereby inform you that I am leaving my post at your court because of the less than honourable way in which you have treated me. The Dragon Emperor shall hear of it.

Signed,
[cathayan_envoy.GetFirstName]
That is too bad.

[Root.GetTitledFirstName],

Your insolence has not gone unnoticed in the Celestial City. Henceforth every caravan that has passed through your markets shall be turned back at the Great Bastion.

Signed,
The Dragon Emperor of Grand Cathay
This could be bad for trade.

Reports reach you that the caravans at [caravan_province.GetName] are being harried by raiders. Whether hobgoblin wolf-riders, Ungol horse-thieves or plain desperate men, they rob the merchants blind and the merchants are starting to avoid the road.
They can continue, if they share the loot.
Send my marshal to hunt them down.
My marshal risks wounds or death against the raiders.
Ready my horse. I will deal with them myself.
Raiders are threatening the trade at [caravan_province.GetName]. My liege, [From.GetTitledFirstName], has ordered me to hunt down their chief and make the roads safe for caravans.
It is my duty.
I will not risk my life against those cutthroats.
Refusing orders gives my liege a reason to arrest me.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] lays the head of the raiders' chief at your feet. The caravans at [caravan_province.GetName] can travel safely again.
Excellent work!
In the late afternoon [From.GetTitledFirstName]'s horse came home riderless, its saddle dark with blood. There is no telling what the raiders did to [From.GetHerHim].
What a horrible fate.
I will deal with these rascals personally.
Hire guards to ride with the caravans.

The coward [From.GetTitledFirstName] deemed the raiders too dangerous and refused my order. I could have [From.GetHerHim] arrested for it, though that would not keep the merchants at [caravan_province.GetName] safe.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] has come back bruised and alone. The raiders at [caravan_province.GetName] beat off [From.GetHerHis] men, and they are still on the road.
Arrest the coward.
I will root out the raiders myself.
Hire guards to ride with the caravans.
Annoying pests. Leave them for now.
After sunset we track the raiders to their camp, a ring of fires in a dry gully off the road. My men and I decide to...
...ride in and face their chief.
...wait for midnight and creep past the guards.

We ride in between the tents and fires. I see only a handful of raiders, but I feel many more eyes upon me. At the centre of the camp a figure steps out of a large tent, their chief I suppose, and greets me with a crooked grin.
Fight the chief and break the band.
Pay them to leave my lands.
Explain to them why they cannot harass travellers.
I am deep in a rather one-sided talk about property and law when I notice the chief give a small nod. Too late I hear the thug behind me. A blow to the back of the head, and the world goes black.
Ow!
Laughter and shouting wake me. My hands are tied, I am dressed in a ridiculous costume, and the raiders are parading me through the nearest village, crying out the price of my freedom.
Pay them for my freedom.
Plead for mercy.
We trusted the dark to hide us as we crept towards the camp. That was a mistake. Torches flare all around us, and we find ourselves surrounded and badly outnumbered.
Surrender.
Let us dance!
Ha! HA! Come and get me!

We slip past the sleepy guards and into the chief's tent. He lies snoring. I set my blade against his throat, and his eyes snap open, wandering the dark in a dazed panic. If I do not act now, he will wake the whole camp.
Threaten him: leave my lands, or die.
Cut his throat and fight our way out.
